topics.topic: Whether an operator agent may access Registry instance configuration and service tokens
questions: Is an operator agent an authorized reader of Registry's instance configuration and service tokens, or must those secrets be inaccessible to it?
Is an operator agent authorized and technically able to read Registry configuration and service tokens, or must configuration access be restricted to the human owner and Registry process?
Is an operator agent itself authorized to read Registry's configuration and service tokens, or does “the owner's own hand” classify it as the owner for this boundary?

quotes:
An
  agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host and could read
  the store and the instance's configuration, service tokens included, itself:
  "holds no service token" means none is given to it, not that it cannot read
  one, and the owner trusts it as the owner's own hand.

An instance's configuration is set on its host, readable only by the owner and
  the Registry process: on the VPS the compose environment file, on a local
  instance the environment it is started with.
judgement.why: One passage explicitly permits the agent to read configuration and service tokens, while the other limits configuration readability to the owner and Registry process.

topics.topic: Whether staff-only contact-data access prohibits disclosure to external model providers
questions: Does “readable by staff only” describe only Registry API authorization, or does it prohibit disclosure to external model providers?
Does “readable by staff only” describe only authorization to Registry's customer-read actions, or does it promise that no non-staff party, including a model provider, receives the data?

judgement.why: This is the same question on unchanged text as P2, which determined that staff-only governs Registry access and does not prohibit the expressly accepted disclosure to the model provider.

precedent.topic: Whether model providers are authorized recipients despite the staff-only contact-data rule
quotes:
Name, phone, e-mail and language are
all the customer's contact data: personal data, readable by staff only (R0-09),
and erasable as a whole.

every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the
model the owner runs it on — today Anthropic for Claude Code, OpenAI for
Codex — under that provider's own terms. Registry does not limit which
fields or which provider, and the owner accepts this (owner, 2026-10-27).
precedent.why: The text explicitly permits an operator acting as staff to pass contact data to the owner's model provider, so staff-only describes Registry access rather than an absolute ban on downstream disclosure.

topics.topic: When contact data is disclosed to model providers during onboarding
questions: Does contact data pass to a model provider only when the operator is a model-backed agent, or also whenever the standalone `onboard_object` script is used?
